passages.provision_quote: This act does not : 1. Create or recognize a right to abortion or alter generally accepted medical standards. The Legislature does not intend this act to make lawful an abortion that is currently unlawful. 2. Repeal, by implication or otherwise, section 13-3603, Arizona Revised Statutes, or any other applicable state law regulating or restricting abortion.
passages.note: Section 2's construction clause disclaims any new right to abortion and leaves Arizona's broader abortion law in force, so the 15-week limit shows only the restrictive side, not a permitted stage.
Diaz voted Yea on House Third Reading of SB1164, a single-subject 15-week gestational-limit bill whose construction clause makes the record direction-only rather than chair-shaped.
Diaz is listed as a co-sponsor of SB1164 (2022); sponsorship evidences the bill as filed, and the same construction-clause rule applies.

rows.reasoning: Diaz co-sponsored and voted Yea on SB 1164 (2022), a 15-week gestational limit with a medical-emergency exception, but Section 2's construction clause states the act does not 'Create or recognize a right to abortion' and does not intend 'to make lawful an abortion that is currently unlawful,' and does not repeal 'any other applicable state law regulating or restricting abortion,' leaving Arizona's broader abortion ban in force. This shows only the restrictive side rather than establishing that abortion is 'allow[ed]... during the first trimester, and after that only to protect the mother's health,' so the record is direction-only.
